subject: chemistry-1
question: Magnesium chloride (MgCl2) is classified as a strong electrolyte. Which statement best explains that classification and the moles of ions released per mole dissolved?

options.text: It dissociates only slightly, so a small equilibrium fraction of ions carries nearly all of the current
It dissociates essentially completely, releasing 3 mol of mobile ions per mole, so the solution conducts well
It dissolves as intact neutral units that reorient in the electric field and conduct by shifting polar bonds
It dissociates completely but releases 2 mol of ions per mole, since each unit gives one cation and one anion

explanation:
A strong electrolyte is defined by essentially complete dissociation into free, mobile ions, which are the charge carriers that make a solution conduct. Each MgCl2 formula unit supplies one Mg2+ and two Cl-, so 1 + 2 = 3 mol of ions per mole of solute. Partial dissociation describes a weak electrolyte (for example acetic acid), and dissolving without dissociating describes a nonelectrolyte such as glucose.

ELI-10: Two ideas are bundled here. First, conduction needs charged particles that are free to move; a strong electrolyte supplies them because it comes apart essentially completely in water. Second, count the ions from the formula, not from the number of ion types: MgCl2 has one Mg and two Cl written into it, so one formula unit yields three separate particles. Weak electrolytes come apart only a little, and nonelectrolytes not at all, which is why their solutions conduct poorly or not at all.
